approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It samples parents from high-score quantiles, creates a fresh field through crossover and short graph-mutation chains, and uses a Gaussian process fitted only to the current session's accepted scores to buy distinct sampled maxima. The GP compares integer counts of local molecular environments. After three batches without a new best score, purchases are restricted to the forty highest predicted means. Real feedback updates the full scored archive and the best sixty-four breeding survivors; unpurchased proposals are discarded.
approach.novelty: Add one observed-endpoint two-batch rollout, jointly with one-batch retention of unpurchased proposals so its modeled next choices remain available. Each possible current batch is valued by its immediate observed improvement plus the improvement of a next batch chosen after simulated first-batch feedback. Unlike the sibling predictor, winner-probability and persistent-controller variants, this keeps the raw GP and graph generator while explicitly pricing an outcome-dependent future purchase. Earlier immediate-improvement and zero-innovation conditioning trials did not test this capability.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has no outcome-dependent future-decision value: FingerprintPosterior.select chooses ten current sampled maxima and Evolution.suggest discards all unselected graphs. All three actual summary.json and run.log files show successful complete Search runs, macro mean 0.607030316211131 and population seed SD 0.030175277546149237. Reading every Parent session log and trajectory gives 435 complete 160-member allocations, 239 non-improving batches and 88 restricted allocations. The 420 overlapping two-batch windows have equal-session mean realized best-score increment 0.027628024236935136. These measured baseline facts are preserved in policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/parent-evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files, which cite and hash each underlying log, summary and trajectory. They establish the behavior to change, not that lookahead is beneficial. The original indexed analyses show why a new discriminator is needed: n-698a02f85be1 executed EI plus calibrated scale and mean-fantasy conditioning but lost 0.05328817319169632 against its own masked Parent; n-645c611d69c8 raised sampled immediate batch utility from 0.0214373 to 0.0284898 on its Student-t Parent but lost 0.0004071597452423396 and reduced full/late generating-parent gain; n-aa9acd2c2043 executed all 3915 zero-innovation projections yet lost 0.04174224825374232 on its exchange-disabled Parent. Their hosts and objectives stay separate. Finally n-61cb8ba305fa removes an active learned correction and recovers the present Anchor exactly: this plan independently verifies byte-identical trajectories in all fifteen Search cells. Its passive mixture still has lower same-paid MSE than GP, 0.01098210970157113 versus 0.011599451325391918, so prediction loss alone does not justify another purchase rule. Exact trajectory reuse is not independent replication or a new winner.

adoptions.applicability: n-698a02f85be1 and n-645c611d69c8 improved their modeled immediate utility but failed endpoint transfer; n-aa9acd2c2043 only used zero-innovation within-batch projection. None tests a future choice that changes with a preceding observed batch. n-61cb8ba305fa strengthens the need to target actual paid endpoint decisions rather than predictive calibration. The rollout explicitly values the maximum observed score and does not substitute an unevaluated recommendation or a nonadaptive q=20 batch.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Joint first-batch fantasy observations followed by a genuinely outcome-conditioned second decision.; Observed-best terminal utility and actual finite remaining budget; no terminal max-posterior-mean substitution.; A reachable retained future action set, independent estimation/evaluation draws and strict separation of fictional and real observations.

deviations.adopted_setting: Adopt observation-conditioned scenario-tree planning, but use a finite shortlist and one greedy follow-up batch instead of continuous jointly optimized full trees. The retained set makes the limited future proxy executable. This is a bounded rollout, not the paper optimizer, pure KG, Kriging believer or simultaneous qEI.
deviations.paper_setting: Use the specific source method and conditions described in the frozen literature review; source experiments are not campaign evidence.
deviations.reason: Address the indexed limitation while respecting the current task, accepted-only labels, code Parent and compute contract.

adoptions.implementation_change: Replace myopic purchase selection with a bounded two-batch receding-horizon rollout whose utility is the best real or fantasy-observed score. Evaluate current candidate batches under joint first-batch fantasies and a nonclairvoyant conditional next-batch policy. Keep the raw GP and fresh generator, and retain unpurchased feasible current graphs for one real step so the modeled future action set is actually available. Register this acquisition-and-availability change jointly.

adoptions.applicability: The code Parent supplies an exact finite raw-count GP and small de novo fields. This organization applies without installing BoTorch; its default terminal posterior-mean utility would answer a different endpoint question.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Separate temporary fantasy conditioning from stage and terminal utility, and choose the future action after the first outcome is known.

deviations.adopted_setting: Use one finite discrete follow-up batch, a fixed shortlist, explicit observed-best increments, and independent inner optimization/evaluation panels; no BoTorch package, terminal recommendation or continuous tree optimizer.
deviations.paper_setting: BoTorch provides a general multi-step tree implementation whose default terminal value is PosteriorMean, corresponding to multi-step knowledge gradient.
deviations.reason: The paid benchmark endpoint is the best observed score, and the issued experiment fixes the horizon, approximation and environment.

adoptions.implementation_change: Implement a local float64 conditional-Gaussian helper in external/observed_rollout.py and call it from FingerprintPosterior.select. The second batch is selected from an optimization panel before a separate evaluation panel is accessed; utility is the maximum observed score.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen planning review and exact position-four adoption/boundaries in policy/scratch/round75-search-policy/literature-adoptions.json. Reopening the primary paper confirms observed-best utility and outcome-adaptive future decisions; reopening the pinned official implementation confirms the separation of fantasy models from utility and that its default terminal mean is a different objective. The PDF title is Efficient Nonmyopic Bayesian Optimization via One-Shot Multi-Step Trees; the frozen review uses a shortened title for this same URL. Adopt the observation-conditioned construction, with the issued finite shortlist/greedy follow-up/one-step carry and independent inner evaluation as explicit deviations. Internal complete counterexamples motivate the real two-batch discriminator, not an efficacy promise. This is a first bounded adaptation on the actual raw-GP Parent, not a repeat of the refuted immediate or zero-innovation mechanisms, no source-paper performance transfers, and no new model asset, dependency, external labels or benchmark data is introduced.

method_change.previous_method: The actual n-cf8d309c06de code fits an accepted-only raw-count GP, generates a fresh graph pool, buys sequential correlated-TS maxima under its stall gate and discards unpurchased proposals.
method_change.proposed_method: Keep the real-data GP and graph-evolution host, replacing final acquisition by a bounded two-batch observed-best rollout jointly with one-real-step fresh-proposal retention.
method_change.rationale: The Parent lacks an outcome-conditioned future decision and reachable unpurchased support. Complete immediate-utility and zero-innovation counterexamples do not test that missing capability; the joint carry supplies the finite future actions that this rollout requires. The result prices the coordinated component replacement, not planning versus carry separately.

hypothesis: Modify the current accepted-GP acquisition and unscored proposal lifetime jointly on n-cf8d309c06de. At a real announcement let D be the complete real accepted archive, b=max observed score, q the announced batch size, r the remaining budget from the protocol, F the unchanged newly generated pool and H the previous one-step carry. Stable canonical union of H followed by F forms the current action set (at most 320 at this profile). An identity already in H keeps its older birth and expires now even if generated again in F; only identities newly born in F can be retained or used as future representers. This implements the frozen no-renewal rule without modifying the fresh generator. Recompute the original current K3/M40 mean gate on the union. Form the original correlated-TS batch on that set, then at most 32 unique one-position substitutions by descending current GP mean replacement order and stable original TS position order. Freeze this shortlist before scoring. For each A use 16 common joint noisy-observation fantasies Y_A. Let b_A=max(b,max Y_A); temporarily condition the original GP on those observations with its actual raw noise variance (score_scale*0.05)^2. Future support is the newly born current fresh identities minus A, never incoming expiring carry. Update the original stall counter hypothetically (zero if b_A>b, otherwise current streak plus one), and apply the original top-forty gate by conditional mean on that retained-only support when the hypothetical streak reaches three. The frozen policy pi2 greedily maximizes conditional expected observed-best improvement of the entire next batch using 16 joint conditional optimization rows; it updates scenario maxima but neither invents within-B feedback nor reconditions the covariance between its picks. After B is fixed, evaluate it using 32 independent conditional rows. Score Q2(A)=mean_outer[(b_A-b)+mean_eval(max(b_A,max Y_B)-b_A)] and buy the shortlist A with greatest Q2, earliest shortlist index on exact ties. The passive one-batch choice maximizes the same outer immediate term only; it and the original TS choice receive no alternative rewards. At no remaining future budget the future term is exactly zero and the active criterion is this same one-batch objective. Only A reaches the evaluator; all fantasies disappear after allocation. Real accepted labels alone enter the GP, survivor population and breeding history. Newly born unpurchased feasible graphs carry for one real announcement and then expire. This joint change predicts a real future-term choice effect and a strict increase in equal-session realized best-score progress over all nonterminal two-batch windows; endpoint gain is assessed separately. Fresh generation at the next real step is intentionally absent from the model, so its competition and actual gate can change which retained alternatives are bought.

finding_summary.headline: Rollout changed paid choices, but two-batch progress and final scores fell
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment rules out missing future availability and absent decision exposure as explanations for this fixed recipe: both worked. Its limitation is transfer from the modeled continuation to real progress. Only 5203 of 67200 modeled future-batch memberships were bought at the next real step, where fresh graphs, changed eligibility and replanning compete with the retained set. In addition, 30464 of those 67200 greedy positions had zero estimated marginal gain and were filled by exact tie order. A search scheme that represents the actual future proposal process and continuation would address that measured mismatch; its benefit remains open.

Progress became somewhat more frequent but smaller: zero-progress windows decreased from 149 to 135, while average positive generating-parent gain fell from 0.0038830 to 0.0030020, and late gain fell from 0.0020241 to 0.0011574. The Molecular assessment and fragment-excluded comparisons show continued local analogue refinement, not universal scaffold collapse: late within-batch count similarity rose from 0.7240 to 0.7348, some favorable scaffold sets broadened, yet molecules above sixty heavy atoms increased from 21 to 107 and none entered a pooled top-score decile. Decoration hopping included an oversized, repeated-heterocycle branch; the sitagliptin leaders favored aromatic variants that missed the Parent’s stronger partially saturated neighborhood. A proposal operator that creates coherent ring/linker alternatives while retaining useful functional-group placement could address that structural limitation, but these associations do not establish causation.

Both borrowed literature elements—outcome-conditioned planning and temporary fantasy/utility separation—operated. The result rejects the registered finite-shortlist, retained-only rollout’s progress prediction under this GP and generator, while leaving broader nonmyopic methods and the separate contributions of planning and carry unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The rollout executed correctly in all 435 allocations. Future batches changed with simulated first outcomes in 378 of 420 nonterminal decisions, and future value changed 225 actual paid batch choices relative to the same-state immediate-only rule. Every nonterminal retained molecule reached the next action set. Nevertheless, mean realized two-batch best-score gain fell from 0.0276280 to 0.0239956 across the complete fifteen-session panel, with all three seed averages lower. This triggers the registered progress falsifier. Final macro score also fell from 0.6070303 to 0.5579676, a delta of -0.0490627 against the required +0.002; seven task/seed endpoints improved, seven declined and one tied. Sitagliptin MPO triggered the protocol paired task-regression rule. All sessions used their full oracle budgets; no technical failure or missing window explains the result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and cyclic-amine families, with reactive halogen attachments, unspecified stereochemistry and persistent size tails
molecular.overall_character: For n-201fe3876d7a, the frozen request marks both Child evaluation and pairing with n-cf8d309c06de complete: five objectives, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations per session including ten supplied initials. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectories were read; no requested paths or task comparisons are missing. This assessment concerns 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules per node, not unpurchased proposal pools or rejected structures. The Child digest has ring-closure rates 0.9563 to 0.9770 and aromatic-token rates 0.9540 to 0.9724; these are string indicators of molecules containing such features, not aromatic atom fractions. Actual structures include substituted indole/indene carboxamides, carbonyl-rich fused N/O heterocycles, quinoline/quinazoline families, medium aza-lactams and saturated cyclic amines carrying aryl groups. Rings and polar atoms are plentiful; consistent chemical tractability is missing. RDKit 2023.09.6 readings of the frozen trajectories find 794 Child molecules with N-halogen bonds, 236 with O-halogen bonds, 79 with acyl-halide groups and 658 with N-N single bonds; flags overlap and do not constitute measured stability, toxicity or synthetic accessibility. The corresponding Parent counts are 888, 162, 8 and 231. Small all-aromatic perceived rings fall from 170 Parent molecules to 30 Child molecules, so difficult topology is not uniformly more prevalent in the Child. Carbon bearing multiple halogens is present in 51 Child molecules and 24 Parent molecules: the available output does not support categorical inability to make that class. The Child has 127 molecules with at most six heavy atoms and 107 above sixty, compared with Parent counts 98 and 21. None of the five pooled highest-score deciles contains a molecule above sixty heavy atoms. No Child molecule has an explicitly assigned tetrahedral centre in the RDKit reading, although 1,785 contain at least one unassigned centre. Explicit charge notation is rare rather than strictly absent: the digest records one charge-marked graph on the first objective, and all Child graphs have net formal charge zero. Neutral drawings do not prove neutral solution microstates. Structural diversity is moderate overall, with much narrower favored scaffold neighborhoods; neither a single universal scaffold collapse nor absence of ring chemistry describes this panel. Synthetic plausibility is a structural judgement, with no synthesis or conformer validation. All high/low comparisons below are descriptive within-objective associations, not component attribution or tests of why purchases changed. Sources: policy/requests/r0075-03-improve-L01-molecular-assess-3c9873a2a43413be.json and policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json, plus the exact paired files listed under each task. Child run-relative trajectory copies are byte-identical to the request-listed staging inputs; the manifest retains their original absolute locations and SHA-256 hashes. Parent trajectories are the published authoritative files. Deciles use 87 of the 870 optimizer molecules pooled across Search seeds; per-seed audits also retain all rows and 29-molecule deciles. RDKit structural flags, typed/generic Murcko scaffolds and stereocentre perception are documented in those audits.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact substituted indole or indene cores joined through a carboxamide to phenyl/pyridyl rings, with methyl/ethyl, methoxy and aminomethyl decoration. Optimizer molecules span 1-43 heavy atoms; the highest-score decile spans 23-27 and usually carries three rings. Seed 0 favors N-fluoro anilides with an N-amino indole and thiomethyl substituent; seed 1 uses an indene carboxamide/aminomethyl family; seed 2 favors a methylated indole carboxanilide. Final rows remain these families. The pooled top decile has 12 typed and 5 generic Murcko scaffolds, exactly the Parent top-decile counts; this is local analogue diversity rather than broad scaffold coverage. These familiar frameworks are synthetically more recognizable than many of their unusual N-substituents. Evidence files (paired Search seeds 0, 1, 2): policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 328 of 870 optimizer molecules and 60 of the top 87. The leader includes both an N-chloro ring nitrogen and an N-fluoro hydroxylamine-like substituent; a high score does not establish a stable drug-like form.
Twenty-six proposals have at most six heavy atoms. Large duplicated heterocycles and single-atom fragments occupy the poor-score tail, despite a narrow favorable size neighborhood.
missing_features: The favorable compact aryl-amide geometry is repeatedly decorated, but only five generic scaffold patterns occur in the top decile; comparably scoring alternative ring/linker arrangements are sparsely demonstrated.

Ordinary, chemically selective polar substitution is not consistently represented among the leaders: favorable functional-group placement is repeatedly accompanied by N-halogen or N-N chemistry. The trajectories do not identify a unique absent target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145; seed 2 evaluation 283, a 25-heavy-atom trimethyl indole carboxanilide with N-Cl and N(O)F motifs, scores 0.4519753205796759. Seed 1 evaluations 160 and 297 exchange amide N-F for N-Cl and both score 0.4387992465191, showing a chemically consequential edit can be score-neutral here. In contrast, the enlarged thiourea/anilide at seed 1 evaluation 12 scores 0.0005383674511498478, and bare F at seed 2 evaluation 269 scores zero. Thus the observed gradient favors a compact substituted fused-ring/aryl-amide arrangement, not unrestricted ring or heteroatom growth. Child best scores by seed are 0.41885833432199493, 0.4387992465191 and 0.4519753205796759; Parent values are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554, with similarly compact aryl-amide chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: This output is strongly seed-dependent. Seed 1 leaders are compact fused N/O carbonyl heterobicycles with aryl/azaaryl appendages, formate esters and carbon-bound fluorine; its best has 32 heavy atoms and six perceived aromatic rings. Seed 2 instead yields an amino-substituted aryl/quinazoline framework joined to a tertiary acrylamide, with a 38-heavy-atom leader and four aromatic rings. Seed 0 repeatedly combines N-methyl carbonyl heterocycles with long polyunsaturated/imine linkers: its best has 82 heavy atoms and its final row 83. Across all seeds the size range is 1-113 heavy atoms, median 38; 100 molecules exceed sixty, 79 of them in seed 0. The top decile is much smaller, 32-55 heavy atoms, with 22 typed and 17 generic scaffolds. Compact aromatic coupling products are recognizable synthetic concepts; the multiply fused and very large polyunsaturated structures are less convincing as tractable end products. Evidence files (paired Search seeds 0, 1, 2): policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl.
liabilities: The large-molecule tail contains repeated carbonyl heterocycles, long polyenes, imines and aldehyde/ester functionality, increasing synthetic and conformational difficulty without placing those molecules in the pooled top decile.

Formate ester substituents and unusual dense ring fusions require chemical scrutiny. Eleven optimizer graphs contain a perceived all-aromatic ring of four or fewer atoms, although this flag is much less prevalent than the Parent count of 85.
Twenty optimizer molecules have at most six heavy atoms and occupy the low-score tail.
missing_features: Seed 0 lacks sustained access to the compact, complementary heteroatom/ring arrangements found in the other Child seeds and the Parent; adding repeated heterocycles and long unsaturated linkers does not reproduce their scores.

The panel does not establish one universally favorable fused-ring core. What is underrepresented is a set of chemically tractable alternative topologies at comparable size, rather than simply more aromatic rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Fragments such as propanal at seed 0 evaluation 270 sit at 0.5. A compact but densely crosslinked carbonyl heterocycle at seed 2 evaluation 20 scores 0.5197421434327156. The seed 1 formate/fluoroalkyl leader reaches 0.625748502994012, while the seed 2 quinazoline/anilide leader reaches 0.6239791691324417. Seed 0 reaches only 0.6059423769507803 with its 82-heavy-atom structure; the 113-heavy-atom structure at evaluation 194 scores 0.6010130079429032. These observations favor particular complementary aromatic/heteroatom arrangements rather than size growth itself. The published Parent seed-0 leader is a much smaller 31-heavy-atom bridged carbonyl/thione heterocycle at 0.8561477222467935; Parent seed-1 and seed-2 best values are 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. That contrast is scaffold-conditioned and does not imply the Parent chemistry is clean: its leader also bears an O-F substituent and a haloether.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score molecules combine cyclic aliphatic amines with two aromatic units and short carbon linkers. Seed 1 has a substituted diazepane attached to fluoroaniline and chlorophenyl groups; seed 0 has an amino-substituted pyrrolidine, carbon-linked sulfoxide and a fused oxygen-containing aryl ring; seed 2 reaches more elaborate bridged/cyclic amine-sulfinamide structures. The top decile has 28-34 heavy atoms, 12 aromatic atoms per molecule and 2-7 perceived rings. Overall size spans 1-103 heavy atoms, median 33. Its 40 typed/30 generic top-decile scaffolds exceed the Parent 20/18, so this output is not merely one aromatic scaffold. The saturated amine and aryl motifs are familiar medicinal chemistry, but stereochemistry, unusual bridges and heteroatom-halogen attachments reduce confidence in the complete structures. Evidence files (paired Search seeds 0, 1, 2): policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl.
liabilities: The top decile averages 1.9310344827586208 unassigned stereocentres per molecule, with no assigned tetrahedral configurations; a single unspecified drawing conceals potentially distinct structures.
Twenty of the top 87 contain O-halogen bonds. Seed 1 evaluation 278 scores 0.9945296025445853 despite a phenolic O-Cl group and a densely bridged oxygen-containing aryl appendage.
Twenty-one optimizer molecules have at most six heavy atoms; seven exceed sixty, and those seven are in the bottom-score decile.
missing_features: Basic-amine-like ring centres are already abundant; their absence is not the gap. The missing chemistry is explicit stereochemical and protonation-state treatment of those ring/linker arrangements. The displayed scores do not independently show that either treatment would improve the objective.
More consistently tractable realizations of the favorable aryl/amine arrangement are not demonstrated across the complex bridged and heteroatom-halogen variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The diazepane at seed 1 evaluation 299 scores 0.9999978758659713; seed 0 evaluation 283 scores 0.9999863854327827 with a non-sulfonylated cyclic amine and carbon-linked sulfoxide; seed 2 evaluation 297 scores 0.9961452658636211. In contrast, the N-sulfonylated pyrrolidine/N-chloro carboxamide at seed 2 evaluation 20 scores 0.00016650955053713697. All 87 top-decile molecules match the aliphatic non-amide nitrogen flag, versus 30 in the bottom 87; sulfonyl groups occur in 47 of the bottom 87 and none of the top 87. This supports an association with available aliphatic amine centres and the two-aryl arrangement, not a blanket objection to sulfur. Parent best scores are 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864 with related amine/aryl chemistry. Seed 1 still ends by evaluating OCl at 0.007885536181035605.

per_task.generated_character: The molecules join fused aromatic systems to carbonyl-rich cyclic nitrogen frameworks. Seed 0 leaders use a propyl/ethoxy carbazole attached to a medium-size aza ring with two carbonyls; seed 1 combines a fused quinoline/diaryl-ether framework with a cyclic diaza-lactam; seed 2 favors quinoline-O-methylene-N-N/aziridine structures attached to a bicyclic imide. Optimizer size spans 1-60 heavy atoms, median 32; the top decile spans 29-35 and 4-6 rings. There are 582 typed and 399 generic scaffolds across the output, falling to 53 and 29 in its top decile; Parent figures are 560/380 overall and 42/22 at the top. This is considerable ring-topology variation with repeated aromatic/carbonyl combinations, rather than absence of polar or cyclic chemistry. Medium rings, fused systems and N-N substitutions make many individual products more challenging than ordinary amide analogues. liabilities: N-N single bonds occur in 189 optimizer molecules and 34 of the top 87, versus Parent counts 128 and 14. Some are hydrazine-like links to strained aziridines; the flag is a context-dependent chemical concern, not a declaration that every N-N compound is unstable.
Twenty-three optimizer molecules contain at most six heavy atoms. No optimizer molecule carries a specified tetrahedral configuration, although many cyclic products have unassigned centres.
Several end-of-budget structures add additional aza rings or reactive small-ring substituents without preserving the best observed score.
missing_features: The relevant carbonyl and nitrogen functionalities are present, but reliable alternative placements connecting them to the aromatic block are not equally represented across seeds. There is no molecule-only basis for naming one required missing functional group.
The favorable size range lacks systematic configuration-resolved, synthetically straightforward alternatives to the medium rings, N-N-linked aziridines and dense imide fusions.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The two seed-0 aza-dicarbonyl/carbazole structures at evaluations 291 and 299 tie at 0.23821530630160656 despite different placement of nitrogen in the medium ring. Seed 1 reaches 0.23482102902718818 and seed 2 reaches 0.20665742838643064. A 20-heavy-atom dense carbonyl/aza cage at seed 2 evaluation 83 scores 0.11802152895971875, while bare N at seed 1 evaluation 185 scores zero. Eighty-five of the top 87 match the nonaromatic amide flag, compared with 24 of the bottom 87. The observable gradient therefore favors the coexistence and arrangement of an extended aromatic block and cyclic nitrogen/carbonyl functionality; ring count alone is insufficient. The corresponding Parent best scores are 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313, using different ring/linker realizations of related chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The favored molecules remain mostly planar, N-rich carbonyl heterobicycles joined to a substituted aryl ring. They carry carbonyl/imine, N-methyl, fluoromethyl, N-fluoro and N-N substituents; seed 2 adds acyl fluorides, while seed 1 also explores a fluorinated cyclobutene appendage. The top decile spans 25-31 heavy atoms and has 15 aromatic atoms per molecule, usually three rings; the full range is 1-47 heavy atoms, median 27. Top-decile diversity is 16 typed/10 generic scaffolds, versus Parent 21/10. The Parent top decile has a similar median heavy-atom count of 27 but fewer aromatic atoms on average and more rings, reflecting more partially saturated cyclic appendages. Familiar carbonyl heterocycles are present, but many substituents are better described as reactive structural variants than ordinary drug-like functional groups. Evidence files (paired Search seeds 0, 1, 2): policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: The highest-score 87 include 61 N-halogen, 55 N-N-single-bond, 14 acyl-halide and 11 O-halogen molecules; these counts overlap. Reactive N-F/O-halogen and acyl-fluoride attachments can accompany favorable objective values.

Thirty-seven optimizer molecules have at most six heavy atoms. The last seed-2 molecule is a 17-heavy-atom truncated heterobicycle scoring 6.300579770552122e-10, so terminal output is not the same as the best retained molecule.
No specified tetrahedral configuration appears even in the partially saturated seed-1 ring variants.
missing_features: Compared with the published Parent high-score neighborhood, the Child leaders underrepresent partially saturated cyclic/linker arrangements at comparable size. Their fully aromatic aryl appendages do not reproduce the Parent scores.

Carbon-bound polyhalogen substitution is reachable but sparse: five optimizer molecules contain a multiply halogenated carbon and none is in the top decile. The evidence does not justify claiming that the generator cannot make it or that adding it is a task-specific solution.

Stable, configuration-defined alternatives preserving the favorable carbonyl/heteroatom arrangement are not demonstrated; no unique absent benchmark-answer motif can be inferred from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 0 evaluation 298, with an imino/carbonyl heterobicycle, N-F and N-N substitution and a fluoroacetyl aryl group, scores 0.5501033884276103. Seed 2 evaluation 261 reaches 0.524254691857589 with an aryl acyl fluoride; seed 1 evaluation 287 reaches 0.4540300661713025. A different 28-heavy-atom cyclic ester/amine structure at seed 2 evaluation 29 scores 3.7310606408180864e-12, and the 47-heavy-atom duplicated heterocycle at seed 0 evaluation 57 scores 3.061097404486899e-21. Bare F at seed 0 evaluation 166 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Thus neither size matching, extra fluorine nor extra carbonyl heterocycles is sufficient: their arrangement matters. Parent best scores of 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813 occur in more partially saturated cyclic variants at comparable size, but these also contain unusual N-halogen/ring chemistry. The comparison supplies an association, not a clean structural substitution experiment.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-201fe3876d7a, fixed three-Search-seed panel and accepted optimizer trajectories: 794 of 4,350 molecules contain N-halogen bonds, 236 O-halogen bonds and 79 acyl halides. The paired n-cf8d309c06de counts are 888, 162 and 8. Several highest-score families retain these motifs. Multiply halogenated carbon is already reachable in 51 Child molecules, so total inability to construct it is not supported. Exact molecules and paired source files are retained in the task descriptions and scoped chemistry audits.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish chemically selective carbon substitution from reactive heteroatom-halogen and acyl-halide attachment.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide local-environment-aware substitution and functional-group construction that can preserve a favorable scaffold while offering ordinary carbon-halogen and polar-group alternatives. Treat reactivity flags as chemical context, with current-session measured outcomes deciding which alternatives are useful; these associations do not identify the contribution of any component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-201fe3876d7a under the frozen Search panel, all 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules lack assigned tetrahedral centres, while 1,785 contain unassigned centres by the documented RDKit perception. The digest independently gives stereocentre_rate 0.0 on every objective. Ring-rich amine and lactam leaders are among those unspecified structures. This establishes an output-representation gap, not a demonstrated reward for stereochemical enumeration.
transferable_gaps.gap: The accepted output never resolves the stereochemistry of the three-dimensional ring and linker structures it generates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make configuration-preserving and configuration-generating graph edits available when the current molecule has resolvable stereocentres, and retain stereochemical identity through subsequent ring/linker edits. Their usefulness must be learned from the same session rather than presumed from the mere presence of a centre.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the complete accepted n-201fe3876d7a Search outputs, 127 molecules have at most six heavy atoms and 107 exceed sixty; the paired Parent counts are 98 and 21. The very large molecules occur outside every pooled highest-score decile, while late proposals still include single atoms, diatomics and severely truncated scaffolds. One seed develops long polyunsaturated linkers with repeated carbonyl heterocycles. These counts describe observed products, not a universal optimum size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated size distribution repeatedly leaves the productive structural neighborhood in both deletion and growth directions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add edit choices that preserve informative ring/linker connectivity during deletion and avoid uncontrolled duplication during growth. Adapt structural size context from the session already being optimized, while keeping compact and larger alternatives reachable rather than imposing one benchmark-specific target size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-201fe3876d7a pooled outputs contain 168-582 typed and 71-399 generic Murcko scaffolds per objective, but their highest-score deciles contain only 12-53 typed and 5-30 generic scaffolds. Some top neighborhoods are broader than the paired Parent, so this is not a universal diversity collapse. Seed-specific families nevertheless differ strongly: compact heterocycles, extended duplicated heterocycles, medium aza rings and aryl-substituted amines occupy separate trajectories. Exact ties also occur among peripheral or ring-nitrogen substitutions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad raw scaffold coverage does not translate into consistently varied, chemically tractable alternatives within favorable score neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically coherent ring, fusion and linker alternatives accessible while preserving useful functional-group placement. Retain more than peripheral substituent permutations within a promising family and measure alternative-family outcomes from current-session observations. Output concentration alone does not prove that a particular operator or purchase rule caused it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-201fe3876d7a, 30 accepted optimizer graphs contain a perceived all-aromatic ring of four or fewer atoms, and N-N single bonds occur in 658 molecules, compared with 170 and 231 respectively in n-cf8d309c06de under the same Search conditions. The decline in the small-aromatic-ring flag is real; it does not erase dense bridging, medium aza rings or N-N-linked strained-ring examples among the outputs. These are structural alerts, not calculated strain energies or synthesis failures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring and heteroatom connectivity are produced without consistently yielding stereochemically and synthetically convincing whole molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support ring edits that respect local geometry and plausible attachment patterns while maintaining access to useful saturated amine and carbonyl rings. Preserve structural provenance so a difficult ring closure can be distinguished from a simple substituent edit, and assess the resulting complete molecules without treating any single substructure flag as proof of infeasibility.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
